title: Google AI Mode
summary:
AI Mode is a search feature used within Google Search. In March 2025, Google introduced an experimental AI Mode within its search platform, enabling users to input complex, multi-part queries and receive comprehensive, AI-generated responses. Under the hood it uses a custom version of Google's Gemini 2.5 model, the latest and most capable incarnation of Google DeepMind's generative AI.

When a user asks a question, Google fans out the query into many sub-questions, running hundreds of searches in parallel to gather information. This query fan-out technique breaks down the question into subtopics and issues a multitude of queries simultaneously on behalf of the user, enabling the AI to scour the web more deeply than a single search can. The results are then synthesized into a single, easy-to-understand answer. AI Mode was initially introduced as an experiment in Google Search Labs in March 2025 and has been available to all US users since May 2025.

AI Mode appears as a separate tab in Google Search, alongside Images and Videos, or directly at google.com/aimode. It differs from AI Overviews, which are shorter AI summaries that appear at the top of regular search results. AI Mode takes this concept further, enabling users to ask complex, multi-part questions and dig deeper with follow-up prompts, providing more comprehensive and context-aware responses.

The AI Mode shopping experience brings together Gemini model capabilities with Google's Shopping Graph to help users browse for inspiration, think through considerations, and narrow down products. Users can try on billions of apparel listings virtually by uploading a single image of themselves, and when they find the perfect item, they can ask the agentic checkout feature to buy it on their behalf with Google Pay. When AI Mode synthesizes information from many websites into a single comprehensive answer, it raises concerns that users may not click through to individual sites, a phenomenon known as zero-click searches.
